transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

I’m here because… I just can’t seem to get things in order anymore. My kitchen table is covered with papers—my husband’s appointment things, church flyers, notes from the senior center, lists I started and didn’t finish. I sit down to sort it out, and I don’t know what to do first. Then somehow the whole day is gone.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy lately?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say that, exactly. I get frustrated, but I haven’t really thought of it as feeling sad or not enjoying things.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or making decisions lately?

Yes… I think so. If the television’s on in the other room, or if people near me start talking at the senior center, my mind just sort of goes with that. Then I look back and I’ve lost where I was in what I was writing or trying to plan.
Have you been feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even if you haven’t been doing much physically?
I’m not sure. I mean, I’m 70, so I suppose I get tired sometimes… but I haven’t really noticed it being the main problem.
Have you been feeling worried or anxious about things lately, especially when you’re trying to focus on tasks?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t really call it worry. I get bothered when I can’t stay with something, but anxious… I’m not sure.
Looking back, have you noticed that you’re not interested in doing things that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, social activities, or even simple daily routines?
I don’t know… I haven’t really thought of it that way. I still do some of the usual things. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a big change, exactly.
Looking back over the past few weeks, have you found less pleasure or interest in activities that you used to enjoy, even things like cooking, reading, or being with friends?
I’m not sure I’d say that. I still do some of those things… maybe not as much, but I haven’t really noticed feeling less pleasure, exactly.
Looking back, would you say you've been feeling down or blue more often than usual, even if it doesn't feel exactly like sadness?
I don’t think so. I mean… I have off days, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down more than usual.
Looking back, have you felt like most things you do, even things you used to enjoy, just don’t seem as interesting or worthwhile lately?
I don’t really think so. I mean, some things don’t hold my attention the way they used to, maybe, but I wouldn’t say everything feels not worthwhile. I haven’t noticed it like that.
Have you noticed that you've been moving or speaking more slowly than usual lately, or on the contrary, have you been more restless or fidgety without meaning to?
More restless, I suppose. I catch myself tapping my foot or rubbing my hands when I’m trying to sit still. Sometimes I shift around or click a pen without realizing it… enough that people notice.
Looking back, have you found that you take less pleasure or interest in most activities, even things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, socializing, or daily routines?
Not really. I mean, I still do things I like when I get myself to them. I don’t think it’s that I enjoy them less… I just don’t always stay with them very well.
Looking back, would you say that most days, you wake up feeling down or in a bad mood, and that it stays with you most of the day?
No… I wouldn’t say most days. I have my moods, but I don’t usually wake up feeling down and stay that way all day.
Looking back, would you say that you’ve been experiencing a noticeable decrease in your interest or pleasure in activities, even things you used to enjoy, most days?
No, I don’t think so. I still enjoy things when I’m doing them… it’s more getting around to them, I guess.
Looking back, would you say that you’ve been feeling fatigued or lacking energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?
I don’t know… not especially. I mean, I get tired, but I haven’t really noticed it being most days when I haven’t done much.
Looking back, would you say you’ve lost interest in things you used to look forward to, even if you still do them sometimes?
Not really… I mean, I still look forward to things sometimes. I can’t say I’ve noticed losing interest like that.
Looking back, would you say that your mood has been consistently low or down most of the day, nearly every day, for the past couple of weeks?
No… I wouldn’t say it’s been consistently low like that. I have my moments, but not most of the day nearly every day.
Looking back, would you say that there have been several days in the past two weeks where you just didn’t feel like doing anything, even things you normally like to do?
I don’t think so… I mean, maybe here and there, but I haven’t really noticed several days like that.
Looking back, would you say that there have been several days in the past two weeks where you felt like nothing was interesting or enjoyable, even things you used to like doing?
I don’t think so. I mean… I still find some things okay. I haven’t really noticed it being like nothing is enjoyable.
Looking back, would you say that you've had a hard time starting or finishing tasks, even simple ones, more often than usual lately?

Yes… lately it feels like even simple things don’t get started. I’ll sit at the kitchen table with all these papers—my husband’s appointment things, church flyers, notes from the senior center, lists I started—and I just… don’t know what to do first. Then the day’s gone and not much is finished.
